THE CANONICAL TINA4_TEST_* SET. See ADR-0038.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. One test PostgreSQL had thirteen names and no two
frameworks read the same set: TINA4_TEST_PG_URL and TINA4_TEST_POSTGRES_URL
both meant the URL, _USER and _USERNAME both meant the user, _PASS and
_PASSWORD both meant the password, _DB and _DATABASE both meant the database.
Twice in one night a test skipped, someone exported the single name that one
framework happened to read, and more tests appeared: TINA4_TEST_PG_URL turned
up 4 Node tests that had never executed, then TINA4_TEST_POSTGRES_URL turned
out to gate 3 PHP sites under a different name. Both fixes were correct and
neither could have been the last, because there was no canonical list to
check against. An allow-list with no single source of truth rots by addition.
This file IS that source of truth, and test_env_contract in each framework
is the gate: it scans that framework's own suite plus .github/workflows and
fails, naming the offender and its file, on any TINA4_TEST_* name not listed
here. Adding a fourteenth spelling now turns a suite RED instead of silently
turning a test off.
THE GRAMMAR is TINA4_TEST_<SERVICE>_<ATTRIBUTE>, mirroring the runtime's own
TINA4_<SUBSYSTEM>_<SERVICE>_<ATTRIBUTE> (TINA4_SESSION_REDIS_HOST,
TINA4_SESSION_MEMCACHED_PORT, TINA4_SESSION_MONGO_URI). The service name
follows the subsystem directly. There is no consumer infix: the runtime has
TINA4_CACHE_URL, never TINA4_CACHE_REDIS_URL, so the cache tests do not get
a TINA4_TEST_CACHE_REDIS_URL either.
ATTRIBUTE spellings mirror the runtime: _USERNAME and _PASSWORD (as in
TINA4_DATABASE_USERNAME / TINA4_DATABASE_PASSWORD), never _USER or _PASS;
_DB (as in TINA4_SESSION_MONGO_DB), never _DATABASE. Mongo's connection
string is _URI because the runtime declares TINA4_SESSION_MONGO_URI
canonical and TINA4_SESSION_MONGO_URL a legacy alias.
ADDING A NAME. Add it here first, in the right service, then use it. A name
that is not here does not exist. If you need a new service, add the service
with the standard attributes rather than inventing a one-off spelling.
These are TEST-ONLY variables. They are deliberately NOT in the tina4 client
CLI's known_vars() (tina4/src/env_config.rs): write_env_example iterates that
manifest, so a name added there is emitted into every user's .env.example.
Runtime configuration lives in known_vars(); test service coordinates live
here.
_fixtures_comment: Test-owned values, NOT service coordinates. CI and lab-env.sh never set
these: a test writes or toggles them to exercise a code path, so they are
on the canonical list but carry no service grammar.
MODE              router error-event test toggles dev/prod
NO_REDIS_DRIVER   forces the driverless cache variant
WRITE_PATH_*      the write-path contract's own database coordinates
FROM_DEFAULT      written into a temp .env to prove loadEnv() reads it
FROM_CUSTOM       written into a temp .env to prove TINA4_ENV_FILE wins
ENV_DB_URL        written by putenv() to prove Database::fromEnv() reads it
_dynamic_comment: Literal prefixes of names BUILT at runtime, which no static scan can resolve
to a full name. Each entry is the literal text that appears in the source
TINA4_TEST_DB_NONEXISTENT_  PHP appends uniqid() to get a name that is
fails on a missing variable. Deliberately
Keep this list at zero-or-near-zero. A dynamic name is a hole in the gate:
the scanner cannot check what it cannot resolve. Prefer an explicit name.
The Ruby queue specs used to interpolate TINA4_TEST_#{backend.upcase}_HOST;
they now use an explicit per-backend map so the gate can see every name.
_match_rule_comment: HOW THE GATE DECIDES A NAME IS BEING USED. All four implement this rule,
and they must stay identical or the gate means four different things.
A name counts only where it is actually USED, which is any of:
(a) immediately preceded by a quote character ' or "
os.environ.get("X"), getenv('X'), ENV["X"], process.env["X"],
putenv("X=value"), and names written as bare string literals in a list
(b) immediately preceded by process.env.
the dot form, which is the dominant read in tina4-nodejs
(c) preceded by 'export ' ANYWHERE on the line, not only at its start
(d) at the start of a line, after optional whitespace - a YAML env key or
a bare shell assignment
Reference regex, multiline:
(?:['"]|process\.env\.|export\s+|^\s*)(TINA4_TEST_[A-Z0-9_]+)
The trailing + is load-bearing: a bare 'TINA4_TEST_' prefix must not match.
(c) MUST NOT be anchored to the line start. All four repos ship an
mqtt-infra.sh that emits its coordinates as
echo "export TINA4_TEST_MQTT_URL=mqtt://127.0.0.1:1883"
and an anchored 'export' misses all five MQTT names in every repo - a name
that is SET and never READ, which is the precise failure this gate exists to
catch. Python had this right first; the other three were corrected to match.
WHY NOT JUST GREP FOR TINA4_TEST_[A-Z0-9_]*. Because that also matches
unquoted prose, and it produced 15 false positives on an untouched tree:
'# canonical TINA4_TEST_PG_HOST / _PORT' yields TINA4_TEST_PG_, and
'the same TINA4_TEST_* values work locally' yields TINA4_TEST_. A comment is
documentation, not a read. Loosening the other way is worse: accepting any
token that is a PREFIX of a canonical name would silently accept
TINA4_TEST_PG_USER, which is one of the exact spellings this file retired.
_scan_comment: Where each framework's gate looks. Relative to the repo root. A TINA4_TEST_*
token found in any of these that is not canonical fails the gate.
Workflows are scanned as well as tests, deliberately. A CI file that SETS a
name no test READS is the exact failure that hid 4 Node tests and 3 PHP
sites: the gate must catch a rogue set, not just a rogue read.
KNOWN LIMIT: the gate only polices the TINA4_TEST_ namespace. A test-service
variable named outside it is invisible to this file by construction. That is
not hypothetical - tina4-ruby's CI set MONGO_TEST_URI while four ruby specs
read TINA4_TEST_MONGO_URI, so the specs fell back to a hardcoded address and
the real mongo service container went unused. Name test service coordinates
